scope: Additive source-backed facts for six exact current Game keys that had zero game_facts rows at staging time. Do not apply to the live database without the normal reviewed import step.

facts.evidence: The Research Center for Game Studies collection catalogs the package under the Mega Drive series and identifies the medium as a Mega Drive cartridge.
The RCGS package record lists Sega Enterprises as the responsible organization/publisher.
The RCGS record classifies the package as both war simulation and turn-based strategy.
The RCGS record gives 1991 as its date variant and attributes the date to Mega Drive Perfect Catalog; only year precision is asserted.

profiles.game_key: Bokura no Kazoku: My Family Growing Up in the 21st Century (Japan)

facts.value: Bokura no Kazoku; English subtitle: My Family Growing up in the 21st Century
facts.evidence: Millennium Kitchen’s official March 2005 archive uses the English subtitle “My Family Growing up in the 21st Century” alongside the Japanese title.
The developer’s official archive calls Bokura no Kazoku “our PS2 title” (弊社制作のＰＳ２タイトル).
Millennium Kitchen’s official works list specifies PS2 for Bokura no Kazoku.
Millennium Kitchen’s official works list gives the release date as March 24, 2005.
The developer’s official works list names Sony Computer Entertainment in the publisher column for Bokura no Kazoku.
The official Google Play listing is for the Android Bully: Anniversary Edition app.

facts.value: War Drum Studios (in conjunction with Rockstar Games)
facts.evidence: The official Google Play listing states that the mobile version was developed in conjunction with War Drum Studios.

facts.value: Includes content from both the original Bully release and Bully: Scholarship Edition; enhanced graphics and redesigned touch controls
facts.evidence: Rockstar’s launch announcement says Anniversary Edition includes everything from the original release and Scholarship Edition, with high-resolution graphics and controls redesigned for touch.

facts.value: Four bonus classes and additional non-storyline missions
facts.evidence: The official Google Play description explicitly lists four bonus classes and additional non-story missions beyond the original release.

facts.value: Android v1.4.311 — 2026-01-21: fixed a crash when downloading game assets
facts.evidence: Rockstar Support identifies the January 21, 2026 Android v1.4.311 update and its asset-download crash fix.
The official Bokujō Monogatari series page lists PlayStation as the platform for Harvest Moon: Back to Nature (牧場物語 ハーベストムーン).
The official Bokujō Monogatari series page lists the Japanese PlayStation release date as December 16, 1999.
Natsume’s publisher announcement identifies this as the first Harvest Moon title on PlayStation in North America and gives November 20, 2000 as its launch date.

facts.value: Nonlinear real-time farming; livestock care; more than 50 characters; village festival contests and recipe collection
facts.evidence: Natsume’s announcement describes restoring the farm, tending livestock, interacting with over 50 characters, nonlinear real-time play, festival mini-contests, and collecting recipes.

facts.value: WizBang! Software Productions, in collaboration with Activision
facts.evidence: Activision’s period advertisement identifies HyperBlade as developed by WizBang! in collaboration with Activision.
The period Activision advertisement carries Activision branding and copyright and presents HyperBlade as its product.
The Activision advertisement specifies availability on MS-DOS/Windows 95 CD-ROM.

facts.value: A future mega-sport combining hockey, lacrosse, and speed-skating, with brutal team competition
facts.evidence: The advertisement describes the sport as built from hockey, lacrosse, and speed-skating and promotes its violent, competitive play.
The ad says “The Drome Opens Summer ’96”; this is an advertised schedule, not confirmation of the retail release date.
Sony’s current PlayStation Store page says Mister Mosquito was originally released on PlayStation 2.
The official PlayStation Store lists the game genre as Action.

facts.value: Play as a mosquito in the Yamada family home and drink blood to survive the winter
facts.evidence: The official store description identifies the player as Mister Mosquito, an uninvited guest in the Yamada home who must drink blood to survive winter.

facts.value: 12 household levels, with stealth and air-combat encounters against the inhabitants
facts.evidence: Sony’s store description specifies 12 Yamada-household levels and stealth or air-combat encounters.

facts.value: PS4/PS5 conversion of the PS2 version: 2024-09-17
facts.evidence: The official PlayStation Store identifies the PS4/PS5 conversion and lists its release date as September 17, 2024.
